facts.statement: The first remains of Poposaurus were discovered in 1904 near Lander, Wyoming.
facts.quote: The first remains of Poposaurus were found in 1904 near Lander, Wyoming.

facts.statement: Maurice Goldsmith Mehl named the genus Poposaurus in 1915 based on fossils from the Popo Agie Formation.
facts.quote: In 1915, paleontologist M. G. Mehl named Poposaurus based on more complete material from the Popo Agie Formation, including vertebrae, hips, and limb bones.

facts.statement: New fossils of Poposaurus were described in 1995 from the Placerias quarry in the Chinle Formation of Arizona.
facts.quote: In 1995, paleontologists Robert Long and Phillip Murry described new fossils of Poposaurus from the Placerias quarry in the Chinle Formation of Arizona.

facts.statement: In 2022, immature remains of Poposaurus gracilis were described from the Doswell Formation of Virginia, marking the first record of the genus in eastern North America.
facts.quote: In 2022, the partial remains (fragmentary thoracic vertebrae and part a right humerus) of an immature P. gracilis were described from the early Carnian-aged Doswell Formation of Virginia, marking the first occurrence of this genus from eastern North America.

facts.statement: Poposaurus lived during the Late Triassic, from the Carnian to the Norian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Triassic (Carnian to Norian),

facts.statement: Poposaurus inhabited the southwestern and eastern United States during the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Poposaurus is an extinct genus of pseudosuchian archosaur from the Late Triassic of the southwestern and eastern United States.

facts.statement: Adult Poposaurus measured about 4 to 5 meters in length and weighed between 90 and 100 kilograms.
facts.quote: With the tail comprising about half the body length, Poposaurus was about 4 - 5 m long and weighed 90 to 100 kg as an adult.

facts.statement: Poposaurus had a laterally compressed body with a long and narrow hip structure.
facts.quote: The body of Poposaurus is laterally compressed, with a long and narrow hip structure.

facts.statement: Poposaurus possessed five sacral vertebrae, which is three more than found in most early archosaurs.
facts.quote: Poposaurus has five sacral vertebrae connecting the spine to the hip, three more than most early archosaurs.

facts.statement: Poposaurus was an obligate biped, walking exclusively on two legs like theropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Like theropod dinosaurs, Poposaurus was an obligate biped, meaning that it walked on two legs rather than four.

facts.statement: Despite its bipedal locomotion, Poposaurus is more closely related to modern crocodilians than to dinosaurs.
facts.quote: However, as a pseudosuchian, it is more closely related to living crocodilians than to dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence from Arizona confirms that Poposaurus was a hyper-carnivorous predator.
facts.quote: Another specimen of Poposaurus from Arizona, PEFO 34865, includes not only postcranial remains but also cranial remains, confirming that Poposaurus was a hyper-carnivorous predator.

facts.statement: Poposaurus is classified as a member of the family Poposauridae within the larger group Poposauroidea.
facts.quote: Poposaurus is a member of the family Poposauridae, part of the larger pseudosuchian group Poposauroidea.

facts.statement: Long and Murry debated the classification of Poposaurus, separating it from rauisuchians like Postosuchus and placing it in the family Poposauridae.
facts.quote: Long and Murry separated poposaurids like Poposaurus, Bromsgroveia, and the newly named Lythrosuchus from rauisuchians like Postosuchus, which they held in the family Rauisuchidae.

facts.statement: A 2011 phylogenetic analysis placed Poposaurus as the sister taxon to the herbivorous Lotosaurus and shuvosaurids within Poposauroidea.
facts.quote: When the specimen YPM VP 057100 was described by Gauthier et al. in 2011, Poposaurus was included in a phylogenetic analysis. Poposaurus was placed within Poposauroidea as the sister taxon to the large-bodied herbivorous Lotosaurus and the shuvosaurids.

facts.statement: M. G. Mehl named the genus Poposaurus in 1915 and initially described it as a well-muscled, light creature that was likely bipedal and swift.
facts.quote: When M. G. Mehl first named Poposaurus in 1915, he described it as "a well-muscled creature light in weight, possibly bipedal in gait occasionally, and most assuredly swift in movement."

facts.statement: A nearly complete subadult specimen, cataloged as YPM VP 057100, was described in 2011.
facts.quote: In 2011, the nearly complete subadult specimen YPM VP 057100 was described.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence shows that Poposaurus had significantly shorter forelimbs than hindlimbs.
facts.quote: The skeleton preserves both the fore and hind limbs, showing that Poposaurus had much shorter arms than legs.

facts.statement: Poposaurus possessed a crurotarsal ankle, a feature typical of pseudosuchians and usually linked to quadrupedal movement.
facts.quote: Unlike dinosaurs, Poposaurus has the characteristic crurotarsal ankle of pseudosuchians, usually associated with quadrupedal locomotion.

facts.statement: Poposaurus had a "pillar erect" hip structure where the hip socket faced downward and aligned directly over the femur head.
facts.quote: Poposaurus also has a "pillar erect" stance in which the acetabulum or hip socket faces downward and is positioned directly over the head of the femur.

facts.statement: Researchers believe Poposaurus had adductor muscles larger than those of dinosaurs, extending along the entire length of the femur.
facts.quote: Poposaurus is thought to have had adductor muscles that were even larger than dinosaurs, as their insertion site runs along the entire length of the femur.

facts.statement: Poposaurus likely used cuirassal breathing, where abdominal muscles compressed the trunk to pump air into the lungs.
facts.quote: In a form of respiration called cuirassal breathing, the ischiotruncus would contract and compress the trunk, pumping the lungs.

facts.statement: Poposaurus fossils date to the Late Triassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Triásico Superior

facts.statement: Poposaurus was a pseudosuchian archosaur that lived in the Late Triassic of the southwestern United States.
facts.quote: Poposaurus es un género de arcosaurio pseudosuquio del Triásico Superior del suroeste de Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: Fossils of Poposaurus have been found in Wyoming, Utah, Arizona, and Texas.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles se han hallado en Wyoming, Utah, Arizona y Texas.

facts.statement: Poposaurus measured approximately 4 meters in length, with the tail accounting for nearly half of that length.
facts.quote: Poposaurus medía cerca de 4 metros de longitud, de los cuales a la cola le corresponden cerca de la mitad.

facts.statement: Poposaurus is estimated to have weighed between 60 and 75 kilograms, with larger individuals reaching up to 90 or 100 kilograms.
facts.quote: Se ha estimado que pesaba entre 60 a 75 kilogramos, y que los mayores individuos alcanzarían los 90 o 100 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Poposaurus had a laterally compressed body with a long and narrow pelvis.
facts.quote: El cuerpo de Poposaurus está lateralmente comprimido, con una cadera larga y estrecha.

facts.statement: Poposaurus possessed elongated pubis and ischium bones, with the pubis ending in a distinctive hook unique to it and some other primitive pseudosuchians.
facts.quote: El pubis y el isquion son alargados. El extremo del pubis forma un distintivo gancho que es exclusivo de Poposaurus y algunos otros pseudosuquios primitivos.

facts.statement: Poposaurus had hind legs twice as long as its front legs, positioned very close together.
facts.quote: Las patas posteriores son el doble de largas que las delanteras y se sitúan muy próximas entre sí.

facts.statement: Poposaurus had five toes on its feet, though the fifth toe was reduced to a small spur located near the metatarsals of the other digits.
facts.quote: Hay cinco dígitos en el pie, pero el quinto está reducido a una pequeña sobrecaña de hueso a la altura de los metatarsos de los otros dedos.

facts.statement: The three central toes of Poposaurus were well-developed, giving the foot a three-toed appearance.
facts.quote: Los tres dedos medios del pie están bien desarrollados, dándole una apariencia tridáctila.

facts.statement: Poposaurus had a prominent heel bone (calcaneum) that protruded from the ankle joint.
facts.quote: El calcáneo sobresale de la articulación del tobillo, formando un talón muy desarrollado.

facts.statement: Poposaurus was an obligate biped, meaning it walked exclusively on two legs rather than four.
facts.quote: Como los dinosaurios terópodos, Poposaurus era un bípedo obligado, lo que significa que caminaba exclusivamente sobre dos patas en vez de cuatro.

facts.statement: As pseudosuchians, Poposaurus is more closely related to modern crocodilians than to dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, siendo pseudosuquios, estaban más relacionados con los actuales crocodilianos que a los dinosaurios.

facts.statement: Poposaurus belongs to the clade Poposauroidea, a unique group of Triassic pseudosuchians that included aquatic forms, sail-backed animals, and beaked species.
facts.quote: Pertenece al clado Poposauroidea, un inusual grupo de pseudosuquios del Triásico que incluye formas acuáticas, con vela en la espalda y con pico.

facts.statement: Two species of Poposaurus are known: P. gracilis, the type species described by Mehl in 1915, and P. langstoni described by Long and Murry in 1995.
facts.quote: subdivision: * P. gracilis Mehl, 1915 (tipo) P. langstoni (Long & Murry, 1995)

facts.statement: The genus Lythrosuchus is considered a synonym of Poposaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: * Lythrosuchus Long & Murry, 1995

facts.statement: It is noted that while both Poposaurus and early dinosaurs were bipedal, this mode of locomotion evolved independently in each lineage.
facts.quote: Although Poposaurus and early dinosaurs were both bipedal, the method of locomotion evolved independently in each group.

facts.statement: The first remains of Poposaurus were found in 1904 near Lander, Wyoming, in the Popo Agie Formation.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos de Poposaurus fueron hallados en 1904 cerca de Lander, Wyoming, en la Formación Popo Agie.

facts.statement: In 1907, paleontologist J. H. Lees described a fossil iliac bone (part of the pelvis) and identified it as belonging to the phytosaur Paleorhinus bransoni.
facts.quote: En 1907, el paleontólogo J. H. Lees describió un iliaco fósil (parte de la cadera), y lo identificó como perteneciente al fitosaurio Paleorhinus bransoni.

facts.statement: In 1915, paleontologist M. G. Mehl named the animal Poposaurus based on more complete material from the Popo Agie Formation, which included vertebrae, pelvis, and limb bones.
facts.quote: En 1915, el paleontólogo M. G. Mehl lo denominó Poposaurus basándose en material más completo de la formación Popo Agie, que incluía vértebras, cadera y huesos de las extremidades.

facts.statement: Mehl concluded that the iliac described by Lees, UR 358, also belonged to Poposaurus, but did not identify it as a phytosaur because the iliac shape was different and it had more sacral vertebrae fused to the pelvis.
facts.quote: Mehl concluyó que el iliaco descrito por Lees, UR 358, también pertenecía a Poposaurus, pero no lo identificó como un fitosaurio debido a que la forma del iliaco era diferente y tenía más vértebras del sacro fusionadas a la cadera.

facts.statement: In 1961, American paleontologist Edwin Harris Colbert performed an extensive description of known Poposaurus material and classified it as a theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: En 1961, el paleontólogo estadounidense Edwin Harris Colbert realizó una extensa descripción del material conocido de Poposaurus y lo clasificó como un dinosaurio terópodo.

facts.statement: In the same article, Colbert described an iliac from the Dockum Group of Howard County, Texas, which he assigned to P. gracilis.
facts.quote: En el mismo artículo, Colbert describió un iliaco del Grupo Dockum de Howard County, Texas, que asignó a P. gracilis.

facts.statement: In 1995, paleontologists Robert Long and Phillip Murry described new Poposaurus fossils from the Placerias quarry in the Chinle Formation of Arizona.
facts.quote: En 1995, los paleontólogos Robert Long y Phillip Murry describieron nuevos fósiles de Poposaurus procedentes de la cantera Placerias, en la Formación Chinle de Arizona.

facts.statement: Lythrosuchus langstoni described by Long and Murry was reclassified as a new species of Poposaurus, P. langstoni.
facts.quote: Lythrosuchus langstoni de Long y Murry fue reclasificado como una nueva especie de Poposaurus, P. langstoni.

facts.statement: In 2007, Weinbaum and Hungerbühler described material again along with two new specimens from the Tecovas Formation of Texas and the Petrified Forest National Park in Arizona.
facts.quote: En 2007, junto con dos nuevos especímenes de la Formación Tecovas de Texas y del Parque nacional del Bosque Petrificado de Arizona por Weinbaum y Hungerbühler.

facts.statement: In 2011, an almost complete specimen of P. gracilis, identified as YPM VP 057100, was found in the Chinle Formation at the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument, Utah.
facts.quote: En 2011, un espécimen casi completo de P. gracilis, identificado como YPM VP 057100, fue hallado en la Formación Chinle en el Monumento Nacional Grand Staircase-Escalante, Utah.

facts.statement: Excepting the skull, most of the Poposaurus skeleton is now known.
facts.quote: Exceptuando el cráneo, ahora ya es conocida la mayor parte del esqueleto de Poposaurus.

facts.statement: Poposaurus is a member of the family Poposauridae, part of the larger group of pseudosuchians Poposauroidea.
facts.quote: Poposaurus es un miembro de la familia Poposauridae, parte del grupo mayor de pseudosuquios Poposauroidea.

facts.statement: Poposaurus was placed within Poposauroidea as the sister taxon to the huge herbivore Lotosaurus and the shuvosuchids.
facts.quote: Poposaurus fue situado dentro de Poposauroidea como el taxón hermano del enorme herbívoro Lotosaurus y los shuvosáuridos.

facts.statement: Mehl noted similarities between Poposaurus and theropod dinosaurs, including hollow leg bones and a deep acetabulum in the pelvis, but did not consider it a dinosaur because each sacral vertebra possessed only one rib (theropods usually had multiple ribs projecting from each sacral vertebra).
facts.quote: Mehl notó similitudes entre Poposaurus y los dinosaurios terópodos, incluyendo sus huesos de las patas huecos y un profundo acetábulo en la cadera, pero no lo consideró un dinosaurio debido a que cada vértebra del sacro solo poseía una costilla (los terópodos usualmente tenían múltiples costillas proyectándose desde cada vértebra del sacro).

facts.statement: Galton noted similarities between the pelvises of Poposaurus, Arizonasaurus, Bromsgroveia, Postosuchus, and Teratosaurus, and grouped them all into Poposauridae.
facts.quote: Galton notó similitudes entre las caderas de Poposaurus, Arizonasaurus, Bromsgroveia, Postosuchus y Teratosaurus, y los agrupó a todos en Poposauridae.

facts.statement: The pubis of Postosuchus was actually a pubis of Poposaurus, which led to the erroneous classification.
facts.quote: El pubis de Postosuchus era de hecho un pubis de Poposaurus, lo que condujo a la errónea clasificación.

facts.statement: Mehl compared Poposaurus with Dolichobrachium, another previously described genus also from the Triassic of Wyoming.
facts.quote: Mehl comparó a Poposaurus con Dolichobrachium, otro género previamente descrito, procedente también del Triásico de Wyoming.

facts.statement: Among the new material were parts of the lower limb, including the tibia and calcaneum.
facts.quote: Entre el nuevo material había partes de la extremidad inferior, incluyendo la tibia y el calcáneo.

facts.statement: P. langstoni differs from P. gracilis by being larger in size, lacking a rim behind the acetabulum, and lacking a hole in the ischium that fits into the iliac.
facts.quote: P. langstoni difiere de P. gracilis en que es de mayor talla, no posee un borde detrás del acetábulo, y no tiene un hoyo en el isquion que encaja en el iliaco.

facts.statement: This specimen includes the forelimbs, hindlimbs, pelvis, ribs, dorsal vertebrae, and almost the entire tail.
facts.quote: Éste incluye los miembros delanteros, los posteriores, la cadera, costillas, vértebras dorsales y casi toda la cola.

facts.statement: Like Poposaurus, the shuvosuchids were bipedal.
facts.quote: Como Poposaurus, los shuvosáuridos eran bípedos.

facts.statement: The analysis found that the ctenosauriscids and the aquatic Qianosuchus were successively more basal poposauroids.
facts.quote: El análisis encontró que los ctenosauríscidos y el acuático Qianosuchus eran poposauroides sucesivamente más basales.

facts.statement: Mehl named Poposaurus in 1915, describing it as a muscular, lightweight creature that was likely occasionally bipedal and certainly fast-moving.
facts.quote: Cuando M. G. Mehl nombró originalmente a Poposaurus en 1915, lo describió como «una criatura musculosa de peso ligero, posiblemente de postura bípeda ocasional, y muy seguramente de rápido movimiento».

facts.statement: An almost complete specimen, YPM VP 057100, was described in 2011.
facts.quote: En 2011, se describió el espécimen casi completo YPM VP 057100.

facts.statement: The skeleton preserves both forelimbs and hindlimbs, showing that Poposaurus had shorter arms than legs.
facts.quote: El esqueleto preserva tanto los miembros delanteros como los posteriores, mostrando que Poposaurus tenía los brazos más cortos que sus patas.

facts.statement: Unlike dinosaurs, Poposaurus possessed the distinctive crurotarsal ankle of pseudosuchians, a feature usually associated with quadrupedal locomotion.
facts.quote: A diferencia de estos, Poposaurus tenía el distintivo tobillo crurotarsal de los pseudosuquios, usualmente asociado a la locomoción cuadrúpeda.

facts.statement: Poposaurus had an 'upright pillar' posture where the hip socket faced downward and sat directly over the femur head.
facts.quote: Poposaurus también tenían una postura de «pilar erguido» en la cual el acetábulo o fosa de la cadera está orientado hacia abajo y se coloca directamente sobre la cabeza del fémur.

facts.statement: Poposaurus is thought to have had a pubioischiotibialis muscle, which is absent in birds and likely also in non-avian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Se supone que Poposaurus tenía un músculo pubioisquiotibial, ausente en las aves y probablemente también en los dinosaurios no avianos.

facts.statement: Poposaurus is believed to have had adductor muscles even larger than those of dinosaurs, with an insertion zone spanning the entire length of the femur.
facts.quote: Se cree que Poposaurus tenía músculos aductores que eran incluso mayores que los de los dinosaurios, y su zona de inserción recorría toda la longitud del fémur.

facts.statement: A hypothesis suggests Poposaurus had an ischiotruncal muscle running from the ischium, across the pubis, to the abdominal gastralia.
facts.quote: La hipótesis presentada es que Poposaurus tenía un músculo isquiotroncal, que iba desde el isquion, en la parte posterior de la cadera, atravesaba el pubis y llegaba hasta la gastralia del abdomen.

facts.statement: In a breathing method called cuirass breathing, the ischiotruncal muscle could contract to compress the trunk and pump the lungs.
facts.quote: En una forma de respiración llamada respiración cuirasal, el isquiotroncal podría contraer y comprimir el tronco, bombeando los pulmones.

facts.statement: Since the 1970s, Poposaurus has been considered a pseudosuchian archosaur, phylogenetically closer to crocodiles than to dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Desde la década de 1970 se ha considerado a Poposaurus como un arcosaurio pseudosuquio, filogenéticamente más próximo a los cocodrilos que a los dinosaurios.

facts.statement: Poposaurus lived from the Carnian to the Rhaetian stages, between 237 and 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Rhaetian (237 to 201.4 million years ago)

facts.quote: Parent group: Poposauroidea

facts.quote: Type species: Poposaurus gracilis

facts.statement: Poposaurus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
